BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www_dilg_gov.ph OILG OPINION NO CO MAY 22 HON. VIRGILIO R. SALIMBAGAT Punong Barangay Barangay Sto. Nino Municipality of San Jose Province of Negros Oriental Dear PB Salimbagat: This has reference to your letter dated 15 January 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion on the following: I. What are the Barangay activities that need to secure a Mayor's permit and what else are exempted? 2. What does the Barangay Project and Local Office mentioned in the Local Government Code, Section 391 subsection (II) mean? Per the representation, the barangay council conducted fundraising activities during the Barangay Annual Fiesta Celebration and the proceeds will go to the purchase of barangay tanods uniforms among others. You represented that on January 5, 2024, the local chief executive of the Municipality of San Jose issued Memorandum Order 002, Series of 2024, which requires a permit for all barangay activities. You then mentioned that the PNP of San Jose attempted to stop the barangay activities such as the singing contest and disco party activities as per the Memorandum Order. Thus, the request for legal opinion. We will answer the queries in one discussion since they are interrelated. At the onset, please be informed that this matter was already settled by this Department in the DILG Opinion No. 144 series of 2022. The pertinent parts of said opinion are as follows: "Well-settled in our jurisdiction pursuant to Sections 444 (b)(3)(iv) and 455 (b)(3)(iv) of Republic Act No. 7160 that only cities and municipalities issue mayor's or business permits Relatively, Section 152 (c) of RA 7160 is instructive as to what activities need the issuance of a mayor's or business permit, to wit: "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

c) Barangay Clearance. - Ng city or municipality may issue any license or permit for any business or activity. unless a clearance is first obtained from the barangay where such business or activity is located or conducted. For such clearance, the sangguniang barangay may impose a reasonable fee. The application for clearance shall be acted upon within seven (7) working days from the filing thereof. In the event that the clearance is not issued within the said period, the city or municipality may issue the said license or permit." The afore-quoted provision is very clear that the mavor's permit is to be issued to anv businesses put up within its iurisdiction to ANY ACTIVITY conducted therein. The mayor's permit is a regulatory measure exercised by the city/municipality pursuant to the delegated police power given by the Congress to the local government units. Considerably, the mayor's permit is issued as an exercise of delegated police power in relation to the promotion of the general welfare of the people in the LGUs. The Sanggunian of the concerned LGUs pursuant to Section 444 (b)(3)(iv) of RA 7160 may enact an ordinance providing the guidelines/procedure as to the requirement, circumstances, and limitations relative to the issuance of Mayor's permit in accordance with existing relevant national laws and issuances as well as jurisprudence relative thereto." (Emphasis supplied) Generally speaking, any barangay activities need to secure a Mayor's permit as the power to issue or grant licenses and business permits is not an exercise of the government's propriety function. Instead, it is an exercise of the police power of the state.l The issuance of licenses and permits by a municipality or city is essentially regulatory in nature. The authority, which devolved upon local government units to issue or grant such licenses or permits, is essentially in the exercise of the police power of the State within the contemplation of the general welfare clause of the Local Government Code.2 However, the Section 391 (I I) of the Local Government Code also provides for exempted activities that require no permit from the mayor, viz: "Section 391. Powers, Duties, and Functions. - (a) The sangguniang barangay, as the legislative body of the barangay, shall: Xxxx (11) Hold fund-raising activities for baranqav projects without the need of securinq permits from any national or local office or agency. The proceeds from such activities shall be tax-exempt and shall accrue to the general fund of the barangay: Provided, That in the appropriation thereof, the specific purpose for which such fund-raising activity has been held shall be first satisfied: Provided, further, That no fund-raising activities shall be held within a period of sixty (60) days immediately preceding and after a national or local election, recall, referendum, or plebiscite: Provided, finally, That said fund-raising activities shall comply with national policy standards and regulations on morals, health, and safety of the persons participating therein. The sangguniang barangay, through the punong barangay, shall render a public accounting of the funds raised at the completion of the project for which the fund-raising activity was undertaken; Xxxx"(emphasis ours) I City Of Bacolod V. Phuture Visions co., Inc., G.R. No. 1920289, January 17, 2018 2 Acebedo Optical Clinic V. CA Page 2 of 3

The foregoing provision explicitly excludes the fund-raising activities for barangay projects from securing permits from any local or national office. Accordingly, Section 391 serves as an exemption to Sections 152 (c) and 444 (b)(3)(iv) of the LGC which requires the issuing of a mayor's permit and/or licenses for any activity that is legitimately for fund-raising purposes. Notwithstanding, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairss.•i OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLDnasm copy furnished: LEOCADIO T.
